title: ROC-AUC vs PR-AUC
interviewAnswer: ROC-AUC measures ranking across true-positive and false-positive rates. PR-AUC focuses on precision/recall and is often more informative when the positive class is rare and practically important.
why: ROC-AUC and PR-AUC are common interview traps because both summarize ranking across thresholds but behave very differently under class imbalance.
intuition: ROC asks how well positives rank above negatives while comparing true-positive and false-positive rates. Precision–recall focuses directly on how many positive predictions are useful and how many real positives are found.
deepDive: ROC-AUC is the probability interpretation that a randomly chosen positive tends to receive a higher score than a randomly chosen negative. With very rare positives, a low false-positive rate can still mean many false alarms, so ROC can look strong while precision is poor. PR curves expose that operational reality. Neither metric chooses the deployment threshold; inspect the operating point and business costs.
math:
TPR = TP/(TP+FN)
FPR = FP/(FP+TN)
Precision = TP/(TP+FP)
Recall = TP/(TP+FN)
workedExample: If failures are 1% of cases, a model can have a small FPR yet still generate more false positives than true positives because negatives are so numerous. PR-AUC will reflect this more directly than ROC-AUC.
code:
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, average_precision_score
print(roc_auc_score(y_true, scores))
print(average_precision_score(y_true, scores))
commonMistakes: Saying PR-AUC is always better than ROC-AUC.
Using AUC as if it were the performance at the chosen production threshold.
Comparing PR-AUC across datasets with very different prevalences without context.
followUps: Why can ROC-AUC look good on imbalanced data?
How do you choose a threshold after looking at the curve?
What happens to precision when prevalence changes?
production: Use the metric that reflects the operational objective, then select a threshold under explicit recall/precision, capacity or cost constraints. Monitor prevalence because it changes precision even if ranking quality is unchanged.

visual.title: ROC and precision–recall views
visual.caption: ROC plots TPR vs FPR across thresholds. For rare positives, precision–recall curves often make the useful trade-off more visible.
